name: Laugh and Lie Down
description: Laugh and Lie Down is the earliest documented European fishing card game, dating back to 16th-century England. Played by five players, it is a game of capture where players aim to win pairs from a central pool. The game's name comes from its most famous mechanic: if a player cannot make a capture on their turn, they must discard their entire hand ('Lie Down') while the other players literally 'Laugh' at their misfortune.

overview.description: Laugh and Lie Down is the earliest documented European fishing card game, dating back to 16th-century England. Played by five players, it is a game of capture where players aim to win pairs from a central pool. The game's name comes from its most famous mechanic: if a player cannot make a capture on their turn, they must discard their entire hand ('Lie Down') while the other players literally 'Laugh' at their misfortune.

history.origins: First recorded in 1522 in a poem by John Skelton ('Why not to Court'). It is mentioned by Shakespeare and described in detail by Francis Willughby in his 17th-century 'Book of Games' (c. 1665), which is the only known historical description of the rules.
timeline: 1594: Referenced by John Lyly in 'Mother Bombie'.
c. 1665: Rules codified by Francis Willughby in his 'Book of Games'.
18th Century: Popular social entertainment for the English gentry.
19th Century: Largely replaced by Casino and other fishing games.
Present: Studied by card historians as the grandfather of modern fishing games.
history.cultural: The name was used as a double entendre in Elizabethan England for amorous encounters. The Oxford English Dictionary notes it was 'frequently used punningly with reference to sexual intercourse.' The game represents the bawdy humor of Renaissance England.
history.evolution: The game's distinctive 'Lying Down' rule was a precursor to the 'Go Fish' mechanic, but much harsher as it removed the player from the round entirely. The fishing mechanic (capturing cards from a pool) influenced later games like Casino and Scopa.

setup.players: 5 players is the standard historical format (Willughby's rules). Easily adapted for 3-6 players.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Ace is low for determining the dealer (lowest card deals).
setup.dealing: Deal 8 cards to each player (one at a time, face down). Place the remaining 12 cards face-up on the table as the pool. The pool cards should be clearly visible but not arranged in any particular order.
setup.equipment: Standard deck and counters for stakes.

rules.objective: Capture at least 4 pairs (8 cards) and avoid being the first to 'Lie Down.' Be the last player with cards in hand to win the largest share of the pot.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Pre-Play Claims**: Before play begins, check your hand for prials (three of a kind) or mournivals (four of a kind). If you have a prial, you may immediately set down two of those cards as a captured pair, keeping the third in hand. If you hold a mournival, you win all four cards immediately. 2. **Play**: Dealer's left-hand neighbor starts. On your turn: Play ONE card from your hand. Use it to capture either ONE or THREE cards of the same rank from the pool. Alternatively, play a PAIR from your hand to capture a PAIR on the table. 3. **Immediate Pair Claim**: If you hold a matching pair in hand, and another player captures a table card of that rank, you may immediately (even out of turn) add your pair to your won cards. 4. **Lying Down**: When you can no longer captureâ€”whether because you have no cards matching any on the table, or because no table cards remainâ€”you must 'Lie Down': place your entire remaining hand face-up on the table as new pool cards, and exit the round.
keyRules: Pair = Two cards of the same rank (A-A, K-K, etc.)
Prial = Three cards of the same rank (pair royal)
Mournival = Four cards of the same rank
If initial pool contains a mournival, dealer wins all four cards immediately.
Each player puts 2 stakes into the pot; dealer puts 3 stakes.
Last player with cards wins 5p from the pot.
Everyone counts won cards. +/- 1p per 2 cards above or below 8 cards.

strategy.basic: Prioritize the central pool. If there is only one card of a rank in the pool, and you have that card, take it immediately! This ensures you don't 'Lie Down' for at least one more turn. Don't play pairs from your hand unless forcedâ€”save them as insurance.
strategy.intermediate: Pair Hoarding: If you have a pair in your hand, don't play it immediately. Save it as a 'buffer.' If your turn comes and no table capture is possible, you can play one of your pair cards to take the other from the table in the next turn (assuming it survives). Watch for opponents' mistakesâ€”be ready to claim uncollected pairs or mournivals.
strategy.advanced: Table Clearing: If you are the leader, try to leave the pool as 'rank-depleted' as possible. If you take the only 7 on the table, the next player who holds a 7 is much more likely to be forced to 'Lie Down.' Force opponents to use their pair cards early by threatening to capture the table cards they need.
tips: Wait for the dealer to take any mournivals from the pool first. Every card taken by the dealer is one less you can use to stay in the game.
Pay attention to the ranks already captured. If all four Kings are captured, a King in your hand is a 'dead card' that will eventually force you to Lie Down.
The player to your left is your biggest threatâ€”watch what they capture to predict what ranks they no longer hold.
If you have a prial (three of a kind), claim two immediately but keep the third as a 'save' card.

scoring.winCondition: Last player with cards in hand wins 5p. Card count adjustments: +/- 1p per 2 cards from 8.

synthesis.shortDescription: The earliest documented European fishing game, where players capture pairs from a pool or 'lie down' when they can't play.
